decision: Create feat/video-reference-upgrades from main
why: The objective requires a new branch
evidence: git log showed main at dca3854 and no prior implementation commits
result: Created the branch without modifying unrelated untracked files

decision: Treat the supplied plan as the phase contract
why: README marks the plan approved and Phase 0 ready
evidence: graphify-out is absent; current source and plan are available
result: Started Phase 0 from the approved fixture and benchmark requirements

decision: Use real adapter renders and a typed JSON evidence schema
why: Later dependency and performance phases need machine-comparable baselines
evidence: parity.json, long-render.json, and timeline-1000.json all report status passed
result: Baseline captures sampled frames, FFprobe data, wall time, RSS, fixture digests, and Studio selection

decision: Keep unrelated test failures as named baseline debt
why: The failing preview test is untracked user work and the API failures predate this phase
evidence: Tracked frontend suite passes with the untracked test excluded; API reports 3201 passing and 37 failing
result: Preserved unrelated files and documented exact reproduction details

decision: Accept Phase 0 after focused review
why: The review corrected mixed-media coverage, independent 5.1 probing, output-audio probing, portable commands, and host-probe resilience
evidence: All three JSON reports pass; browser acceptance passes; tracked frontend suite passes; lint and syntax checks pass
result: Ready for an atomic Phase 0 commit with unrelated workspace files excluded

decision: Pin Remotion 4.0.522, mediabunny 1.55.5, zod ^4.5.4, HyperFrames 0.8.31 together
why: The plan requires one resolved copy per package so render fixtures stay reproducible
evidence: pnpm why reports a single mediabunny@1.55.5, a single zod@4.5.4, and remotion@4.0.522 across all manifests
result: Exact pins landed in all three manifests plus packages/video-ir

decision: Re-measure the acceptance baseline after pnpm install, not before
why: The first phase-1 evidence was captured against a node_modules tree still on 4.0.515, so it did not measure the bump
evidence: Installed tree reported remotion 4.0.515 while the reports claimed 4.0.522
result: Re-ran parity and long-render against the real installed tree

decision: Treat the +79.68 percent peak-RSS run as a cold-start artifact, not a regression
why: Two warm repeats measured -1.38 and +2.42 percent with no code change between them
evidence: long-render.json and long-render-repeat.json, both compared to phase-0
result: Published a warm run as evidence and documented the discard-first-run rule

decision: Prove the packaged-sidecar contract with a new scripts/video-sidecar-probe.mjs
why: Plan item 10 needs a real packaged binary reporting typed unavailable reasons, and no harness existed
evidence: darwin-arm64 binary answers /video/engines with not-found and browser-missing; linux-x64 bundles and audits, runtime deferred to a linux runner
result: Both reports committed; the linux runtime probe is a named, reproducible gap

decision: Do not adopt hyperframes-localize-fonts
why: Its adoption is conditional on cross-host font drift, and the fixture shows none
evidence: parity.json SSIM improved slightly across the bump with no font-shaped difference
result: Deferred until a second host exists to compare against

decision: Ignore machine-generated evidence JSON in oxfmt
why: oxfmt collapses arrays the report writers expand, so formatting them makes the next run dirty the tree
evidence: format:check flagged phase-0 and phase-1 reports the harness had just written
result: Added dev-doc/**/evidence/** to .oxfmtrc.jsonc ignorePatterns

decision: Carry the 144-versus-84 render-input failure into phase 2 rather than fixing it here
why: It reproduces identically on the pre-upgrade tree, so it is not a bump regression, and phase 2 rewrites the derivation it covers
evidence: Stashing the manifest changes reproduces both failures; 103 of 104 API video unit files pass
result: Recorded in the phase-1 evidence README as carried baseline debt

decision: Apply the output range in compileTimelineToEdl rather than per engine
why: The EDL is the one seam Remotion, HyperFrames, and the HTML fallback all read, so the exit gate holds by construction
evidence: timebase-range.json passes render-local-time-starts-at-zero and clips-outside-range-dropped through the real compile path
result: One implementation instead of three that could drift

decision: Store NTSC rates as exact fractions and snap observed decimals to them
why: A probe reports 29.97, which normalizes to 2997/100 and drifts against the real broadcast rate
evidence: timebase.test.ts asserts 23.976 and 29.97 derive to 24000/1001 and 30000/1001
result: snapObservedFrameRate in the IR is the single place decimals become rates

decision: Keep the numeric fps as a derived compatibility field
why: Old documents and older builds read it, and the plan forbids deleting it in this phase
evidence: compatibilityFps emits 29.97 for 30000/1001; the acceptance checks compatibility-fps-preserved
result: Rational rate is the source of truth, the number is an echo

decision: One setOutputRange op covers set and clear
why: The inverse of a set is a set to the previous value, so a separate clear op would only duplicate inversion logic
evidence: timeline-ops.test.ts round-trips set, replace, and clear through applyTimelineOp
result: Undo works for the range like any other timeline edit

decision: Fix the stale 144-frame assertions rather than the implementation
why: Commit 034a0be deliberately made picture own render duration; the test was left behind
evidence: The failure reproduces identically on the pre-upgrade tree, and the commit message says so
result: Phase 0 baseline debt closed with the reason recorded in the test

decision: Extract playhead actions into a hook instead of raising the component-size ceiling
why: The allowlist is a downward ratchet; raising current would move it the wrong way
evidence: Timeline.tsx is back to 371 lines and check:component-size passes
result: Split, marker, frame step, and In/Out now share one hook because they share the playhead anchor

decision: Share the half-open window predicate with the API rather than writing a second one
why: The plan names a second subtly different definition as the risk; clipIntersectsWindow mirrors intersects exactly
evidence: timelineClipWindow.test.ts asserts both boundary cases the API predicate defines
result: One definition of "in the window" across frontend and backend

decision: Carry a running maximum end time in the clip interval index
why: Without it a long clip near the timeline start forces a full scan on every pointer move
evidence: timeline-1000.json p95 0.0080ms across twelve tracks; the long-clip case is covered in timelineClipWindow.test.ts
result: Backward walk stops as soon as no earlier clip can reach the window

decision: Split pinning between the shared hook and TimelineTrack
why: Only the track level knows link-group membership and which track is the drop target
evidence: timelineRenderingPerformance.test.tsx covers selection, link partners, and drop-target pinning separately
result: Each level pins what it can actually see

decision: Test windowing against TimelineTrack, not the whole Timeline
why: The row virtualizer measures through ResizeObserver, which the test setup stubs as a no-op, so a full Timeline render mounts no rows at all in jsdom
evidence: A debug render of Timeline with 1000 clips produced zero track rows and zero clips
result: Component-level test observes the contract the virtualizer would otherwise hide

decision: Measure the shipped query through tsx instead of reimplementing it in the benchmark
why: A copy in the .mjs harness would drift from the module it claims to measure
evidence: timeline-1000.json reports indexedMatchesLinear true, comparing the shipped query against the Phase 0 linear scan on every window
result: Benchmark measures queryClipWindow itself

decision: Report the browser interaction budget as a named gap rather than inferring it
why: Pointer latency and dropped frames need a production browser harness this phase does not add
evidence: The benchmark's limitations field names exactly what is unmeasured
result: Structural DOM bound is proven; the paint-level budget stays open with repro steps
